"I feel bad, Cas. He keeps telling me it's fine and we should keep going all night, but he's clearly tired from all the activity before I am! It's been two weeks of this, should I tell him that we should stop?"

Castorice opens her mouth, then closes it. She takes out a notebook and a pen to scribble something down, before turning back to him.

"…What exactly are we talking about here?"

"Mydei's stamina! Apparently, it's been harder for him to keep up with me without his immortality! Do you think I've been too rough with him?!"

Phainon is met with reminders that Mydei no longer has his flaw of immortality. The realisation is more significant than he had expected.

chapters.html:
The end of their journey still feels like a dream, sweet and hazy and to be broken at any time. Phainon feels the weight of the world lifted off his shoulders; joy and laughter filling this eternal land that they've created. It's an odd feeling to not have to wield his blade any longer, the grip of his hands usually made for battle now loosened and unaccustomed.

Sometimes, as he walks around the garden, seeing a bright horizon that no longer has to be lit by him, Phainon wonders when he would wake up from this dream. Pink leaves fluttering on their branches stretch past the skies, the pale hues of their new world a stark contrast to his sombre domain. His body feels light—too light—like he's not truly there.

But each of his footsteps land firmly on the turf beneath him. He can smell the fresh air, the scent of flowers. He hears the splashing of water from the fountain of their memories, Amphoreus' memories.

A part of him is terrified that this is all real. That after every cycle he's gone through, each agonising step along this endless path, he's finally reached a place where he doesn't have to walk any longer.

And with nothing left to bear—with Amphoreus no longer needing their Deliverer—what is Phainon meant to do?

The dawn rises above him without Kephale's hands. The world ticks forward without the Deliverer pushing them towards the Era Nova. Phainon has been born each time with a prophecy in his heart. Who is Phainon without this unbearable weight? What does he want, that no one else could possibly intrude on?

He sees the other Heirs already deciding on building their lives right from the beginning—actions, not words. Words that dance on Phainon's lips, but unable to move in tandem.

Their care and worry is extremely appreciated, but there's still things Phainon feels like he needs to shield away from them. Like that gaping hole in his chest that can't be filled by Amphoreus' rejoice, or the burn of his hands that continue to desire battle. Destruction consumes him to the core, no matter how hard he tries to push it down.

The Trailblazer tells him to find new ways to feed his restlessness. Phainon's attempted them all, he swears—cooking, smithing, knitting; the Market must be sick of his pestering to try their jobs—but nothing keeps him in place for long.

Now, he's pacing around the courtyard while people are still rousing from sleep, mind wandering far and wide for things to do.

"I was wondering where you'd run off to."

Phainon cocks his head to the entrance of the garden, a smile creeping to his face. The expression on Mydei's own is unamused; his clothes seem to be messily thrown on, rather than its usual neat presentation.

"Mydei. I'm honoured to hear that you're looking for me right as the Entry Hour ticks in. Desperate much?"

Mydei scoffs, crossing his arms, bare, no golden gauntlets to be found, over his chest. "I was seeing my parents off, before Cipher told me that there's a 'puppy skulking around the gardens'. Her words, not mine. I figured I should make sure everyone's beloved saviour doesn't overthink himself into exhaustion before the Lucid Hour."

Phainon huffs under his breath, turning back to watch the sky. "I'm doing fine, just a bit of reminiscing. Are you not heading back to Castrum Kremnos with them?"

"There are Kremnoans who have decided to stay in Okhema. I've also chosen to stay alongside them. A bridge between Kremnos and Okhema should still be held, even if the Black Tide is no longer a threat."

"Is this duty, or your own will?" Phainon spins around to return Mydei's stern gaze.

Mydei doesn't hesitate as he says, "You must have a twisted version of me in your head from your memories, if you believe me to do anything I did not wish to. I've spent much of my time in Okhema through the countless cycles, I don't see why it's odd I wish to stay here."

Phainon sighs, a smile gracing his face. "I guess I shouldn't be surprised."

The wind of the morning sun is more blissful than he could ever imagine. Mydei's hair ruffles through the direction of the open skies, golden like wheat fields and red like the large red pomegranate fruits hanging from Kremnos' trees. Yet, Mydei smells like myrtles and tart citrus, his hair carrying a trace of sandalwood and jasmine.

And with the wind carrying his hair over his shoulders, Phainon spots a bruise beneath Mydei's left clavicle. It's darkening into an irregular spot of ugly purple on his pale, pristine skin, the red ink that curls around his neck ruined along the edge. If Phainon tries to throw it a guess, he'd say that Mydei had accidentally knocked into something just this morning, and hadn't bothered with covering it up.

And of course he wouldn't, he never had to. Mydei is always pristine and unmarred, even when he's covered in the glistening gold of his blood. Cuts; stabs; bruises, they never stay long. Fading away like they never existed in its entirety.

It's ethereal. It's enthralling. Phainon bears his own scars like trophies, but seeing Mydei's perfection has always ignited a fire in him. A man who bathes in strife, yet his body does not show any of it.

But now, that bruise does not disappear like a faded thought. It lingers. It makes Mydei look too vulnerable, too real for Phainon to reach for.

"You're hurt," Phainon says, eyes fixed on the bruise.

Mydei follows his gaze downwards. "Ah, I swung a cabinet door onto myself. It's taking a while to heal."

"It's taking a normal amount of time to heal," Phainon reminds him. His heart feels ready to burst from his rib cage with how quickly it pumps. "Let's go and patch that up."

"No need for that. It'll heal eventually."

Mydei is stubborn to a fault. It makes Phainon want to scream sometimes—not out of frustration, but the knowledge that they're exactly the same on the inside. This time, that stubbornness works in his favour, like an unstoppable force standing in the way of this immovable personality.

"Yes, with some salve and a bandage. Like how everyone's bruises do. I have some at my place; be thankful I'm not dragging you to Hyacine."

Mydei doesn't move. "Bruises heal on their own. My previous accelerated healing was not a sort of magic, but mere acceleration. I don't need to change anything."

"That acceleration is long gone, so it wouldn't hurt for you to use medicine as an alternative form." Phainon steps closer, the desire to reach out to touch Mydei's skin gripping his throat. "It's too obvious of a bruise. Covering it up would ease people's hearts."

While his words are even and tactful, Phainon wonders how well his own marks would stay on this mesmerising body. The dig of fingertips against that lithe waist; lovebites scattered across shoulders and naps; the reddening scar of teeth sinking into lips from a heated kiss, it all plagues Phainon's mind like a vice holding him down.

He's lost in his own mind, the intruding thoughts of having Mydei so intimately in an unfitting place to be. Phainon barely catches Mydei's reply when he says, "Fine, only if it gets you to cease your complaints."

Graceful blonde hair falls onto Mydei's shoulder, hiding the bruise from Phainon's eyes. Mydei has started to keep his hair longer—that unruly mane that once halted right beneath his cervical now slides past the length of his thoracic spine, the expanse of red like a tumultuous waterfall. The braid that once sits neatly on his right shoulder now reaches his abdomen, the lock held together by a gold hair cuff that now swings around his waist.

"Lead the way, then. Or do you plan on moping here forever?"

Phainon's back straightens, his legs moving before his mind. "Right, of course. Come along."

Okhema looks as radiant as ever without plight looming upon them. Prosperity is heavy in the voice of the people, finally unbound by fear and apprehension. As Phainon and Mydei weave through the plaza to get to the palace, met with the greetings and adoration at every turn. It's easy to meet those kind words with a proper smile, charming and boyish as he's always been. Mydei bows his head with a blank expression, eyes flicking from the crowd to the way to the way to Phainon's place.

Mydei walks behind him as they make their way out of the crowd. His hand is hooked onto Phainon's cape, keeping them in nearly pressed up against each other. Phainon's breath is rarely this heavy, even when he's sparring with Mydei for hours on end.

"Surely there was a less crammed path to your place. For all your concern about not letting anyone see my wound, it's a little contrary to take me through the market." Mydei's voice tickles his ear, a dreamy baritone caressing his eardrums.

Phainon suppresses a groan as he gets them out of the busy street. "My apologies, my prince. Considering that back entrance is currently blocked by shipment, perhaps we should have gone around and scaled the walls instead."

"I could scale the walls," Mydei mutters, moving to step beside Phainon.

Phainon decides that acknowledging that would only cause a headache and a half. He bats Mydei's arm down when he's pointing at the brick walls, taking his wrist and dragging him out of sight.

"No one's scaling any walls." There's a few flights of stairs to go through after they enter the private residence of the Chrysos Heirs. "Besides, didn't you get injured by a cabinet of all things? I don't trust you to scale four floors without falling at least once."

"I'm not injured. It's just a bump."

"You got bruised by a cabinet. I've seen dromases less clumsy than you."

Phainon is unable imagine how it would have occurred. Surely Mydei knows not to open a door while being in its way, even if he has advanced healing to rely on?

"I hadn't used the kitchen in the Kremnoan detachment's quarters before. How am I supposed to know that their equipment is much shorter than I'm used to?"

"With your eyes, maybe," Phainon says, taking two steps at a time. Their shoulders brush against each other at a turn, Mydei's bare shoulder pushing against the thick fabric of Phainon's attire. "Most people don't let doors hit them in the face."

"Now you're just exaggerating for the sake of it. I've suffered worse."

"Like death?"

"Exactly."

Phainon pokes Mydei where the bruise lies, watching him wince at the ache. "Not exactly. Let's keep the unnecessary sacrificial tendencies to a minimum."

The medical kit Phainon keeps in his house is close to the entrance. He tries not to bother the healers if it isn't necessary, which ends up with him trekking gold through half his home if he were to leave it in the bathroom as he once used to.

Mydei undoes his boots as Phainon goes to rummage through the wooden box. He had restocked on bandages quite a while back, but the lack of… well, anything going on these days, it had gone untouched for ages. Picking out a jar of healing salve and an adhesive bandage, Phainon gets up with a grunt to see Mydei already on his kline.

The allure of Mydei when he's relaxed cannot be put into words. There's that air of aristocracy around him, as one would expect, but not stiff in the regality of it all. It's more laid-back and inviting, the grandeur radiating power rather than sloth.

His legs are stretched out on the flat mattress, and an arm crossed behind his head on top of a decorative pillow. His hair fans out like a bound sheaf, hanging down the side of the kline to brush against the floor. The bruise is now properly exposed, still that dirty purple instead of pale, even skin.

"It's barely the end of the Entry Hour, are you already sleepy?" Phainon sits on the ground in front of Mydei, brushing aside the silky hair. It falls between his fingers like rushing water—or the thick golden blood that flows in both of their veins.

Mydei's eyes are shut; he tilts his head away from Phainon for him to examine the injury. "Just resting my eyes. Get on with it."

The herbal scent of camphor and eucalyptus seeps out in waves as he opens the jar. He takes a finger to the ointment, the cooling sensation of the jelly meeting his skin. It's specially created by the Twilight Courtyard to accelerate the healing of more minor injuries, which Phainon has used countless of times on the scars gathered on his legs and arms.

Mydei's skin burns beneath his touch, even with the salve between them. Phainon watches the twitch on Mydei's face as he spreads the ointment over the bruise, the furrow of his eyebrows when Phainon presses down a little too hard. The soft exhale escaping his lips when Phainon's finger leaves his body. The medicine melts into his skin, leaving its oily residue; Phainon covers it up with the bandage before he stands back up, eyes lingering on Mydei's lying form.

"This was unnecessary," Mydei mutters, pushing himself upright. "It'll still take ages to recover."

Phainon has to suppress the urge to ruffle Mydei's hair. "It takes a normal time to recover. I'll replace the bandage after our bath."

"How presumptuous." Mydei gets to his feet with a stretch of his back, arms raised in the air.

He doesn't leave—he never does, as long as he's already been invited in. Mydei introduces himself to Phainon's kitchen while he's busy repacking his medical supplies, and Phainon can only hope he doesn't end up with another wound from it.

"I'm very much against using Dawnmaker."

"I'm not. Use your blade, or I'll use it for you."

Phainon squints at Mydei, trying to make out if that threat was a joke or not. Examining his expression brings him no enlightenment, because the man is as stoic as a board when it comes to battle.

"I don't care if you're using your gauntlets," Phainon says, as patiently as he's able to muster, "but I will not wield Dawnmaker against you. I'll even use one of those iron training swords if you want."

Mydei fits into the vision of a battlefield perfectly. Broad shoulders and clad in gold armour, muscle rippling through his body under years and years of training. He paints the picture of an undefeated warrior prince as flawlessly as one would imagine, crimson and gold sweeping through the dull background.

It's dazzling to Phainon's eyes. Which is why he refuses to stain that beauty with the blade meant for Destruction.

"Those blunt blades will do nothing against me," Mydei huffs, his arms crossed.

Phainon slaps a hand over his forehead. "Yes. That is the point."

If there's one thing that no one would believe Phainon on, it is that Mydei is unbelievably childish for a man as reliable as him. There's the foolish competitive strokes that Phainon likes indulging in with him, and there's the unrelenting stubbornness over something trivial.

In fact, Phainon rarely uses anything outside of a training sword when it comes to their spars. This is the first time Mydei has ever complained about it, and Phainon has an inkling as to why.

"Are you trying to prove something here?" Phainon asks, reaching for a well-worn greatsword that fits his grip. "I assure you you'll gain nothing by getting yourself hurt."

Mydei's cheeks are puffed as he frowns. "I'm not trying to do anything. Don't make any excuses when you lose."

The clash of metal is a melody to Phainon's ears. Their footwork like a dance in a majestic ballroom, their swings and punches like following a pre-written choreography. Mydei is his balance, his equal and counterpart, for Phainon's erratic song and dance. His blade meets the metal on Mydei's left forearm, a solid punch lands on his own left. The strain is felt in every of his limbs, active muscles aching with use. It's a pleasant sort of pain, one that reminds him that his heart beats in his chest, that he's able to stand in front of Mydei as he always wish to.

He remembers the many times he met Mydei in that week-long clash. It hadn't been in every cycle, as far as he recalls, but often enough to be ingrained cleanly into his mind. Phainon desires to feel that adrenaline rush through his body again, making him move even while everything else in him protests not to.

Normally, they wouldn't have the time to indulge in such a thing. There's always work to be done as a Chrysos Heir back then, expeditions and political meetings consuming their day. Now, Phainon can sink in the heat of their spars with worries erased from his mind, eyes fixed on Mydei and solely Mydei.

He's captivating like this, sweat dripping from his chin and that fierce gaze that shines like the dawn. His lips are parted, his breath heavy and loud. Phainon's hand meets Mydei on the abdomen, a forceful blow that sends Mydei backwards, leave red in its wake.

There's no telling how long they go at it. Phainon dropped his weapon some time in, opting to face Mydei with his bare fists and a grin on his face. The dusk approaches as the day trickles by, still an unusual feeling for the people of Amphoreus. But Phainon doesn't falter with his attacks, and Mydei doesn't surrender so easily. The sounds of battle rage on; Phainon feels his body roar with exhilaration, his mind lagging behind his own movements.

Despite the haze of exhaustion that clouds his thoughts, Phainon can tell that something's off. His fists meet skin more often, Mydei's usually composed posture is now more slumped and innate. The attacks he throws seem to be based on pure instinct, even when he should know that he's given Phainon an opening.

The sky is pitch-black, with stars scattered in its midnight expanse, when Phainon catches both of Mydei's wrists with a single hand. Mydei's body reacts as he would expect—trying to throw him off with his feet planted sturdily on the ground—except he lacks the strength to succeed in that affair.

Phainon drags them both to the ground, relishing in Mydei's grunt of pain as he lands on his back. With his knees on each side of Mydei's chest and his hand over Mydei's head, Mydei is pinned down like a taxidermised butterfly in the cement floor. His hair is tangled beneath Phainon's hands, its softness lost in their brawl.

From this angle, Phainon can see the way Mydei struggles to breathe, his eyelids fluttering and his face drenched in sweat. There are bruises and cuts scattered across his body in a way Mydei's never carried before, dried gold splattered on his chest and arms.

"You should have told me you were worn out," Phainon says, his voice hoarse. "If we keep this up until the Action Hour, people will think I attempted murder on you."

Mydei is breathing heavily as he glares at Phainon. Even with the lack of light, Phainon can tell that his cheeks are flushed pink, and he's gone completely boneless on the floor.

"…I can keep going."

Mydei wriggles his hands, but just Phainon's single grip is enough to hold him still.

"Get up, then."

"You're heavy," Mydei mutters, looking away.

Phainon's barely resting his weight on Mydei, out of concern about irritating the wounds any further. He can see the fatigue on Mydei's face, etched in his expression no matter how he tries to hide it.

Phainon sighs. Stubborn indeed. "Let's head back and get patched up, Mydei."

"I'm fine."

He presses a finger to an open cut on Mydei's cheek. The yelp that falls from his mouth is terribly cute, Phainon decides, like messing with a stubborn child.

"It's either you come with me or I wake Hyacine up to deal with you. Whose nagging do you want to listen to?"

Mydei scrunches up his face while he's dragged to his feet. They're basically trembling, Phainon notes. Like a newborn dromas.

"You scoundrel. Lowly, swindling scoundrel."

"Calling me names isn't going to stop you from collapsing if I let go of you here," Phainon snorts. He has Mydei's arm around his shoulders, holding him up as they walk towards Phainon's residence. "I didn't realise… your stamina was been affected by your immortality."

Mydei seems half-asleep as he leans his weight against Phainon. "I suppose it makes sense that my endurance inherited some of my regenerative abilities too… It's not something I put much thought into."

"Now I feel bad going all out against you," Phainon teases. "It'd be no fun when all you do is lose against me, huh?"

"HKS, don't spout nonsense." Mydei's fingers dig into his scalp, the blunt edges of the gauntlets pushing into his skin. "I'll beat you next time."

The gathering of scars on Mydei's body is progressive, but rapid in its pace.

Mostly because of Phainon, they'll both admit. All because of Phainon.

Mydei insists they spar everyday, which ends up with them limping home in the middle of the night with Mydei drained of energy against him. Phainon would wash and bandage all the injuries that marred Mydei's body with gentle hands, before dealing with his own wounds and promptly passing out.

Hyacine seems completely unimpressed—for the first time, with Mydei and not him—when she sees the ruins of his body. She tries the recommendation of getting him to put on a shirt, which Mydei immediately refutes, thankfully. Phainon doesn't think he'd be able to win their next spar when he's plagued with grief from the loss.

"I feel bad, Cas. He keeps telling me it's fine and we should keep going all night, but he's clearly tired from all the activity before I am! It's been two weeks of this, should I tell him that we should stop?"

Castorice opens her mouth, then closes it. She takes out a notebook and a pen to scribble something down, before turning back to him.

"…What exactly are we talking about here?"

"Mydei's stamina! Apparently, it's been harder for him to keep up with me without his immortality! Do you think I've been too rough with him?!"

The scenery of the Sunlit Garden is truly gorgeous. Castorice had taken the initiative to invite Phainon to lunch there, an array of snacks spread out on the mat while they look out at the endless sunlight.

"Too rough with him…? I mean, if he doesn't mind, I guess it isn't a problem…" Castorice's face flushes, as pink as the guava juice she brought.

Phainon takes a bite out of a sandwich before he says, "Yeah, but he's really stubborn about it, don't you think?" Castorice chokes on her drink, turning away to let out a cough. "He keeps telling me that he can handle it, even when he's gone limp and half-asleep!"

"Uh— Okay…?"

"Then he'll sleep like a rock in my bed, and when he wakes up he insists that we go again!" Phainon cries, nearly dropping his sandwich. "But he gets mad whenever he loses, even though he's the one who initiated our spar!"

"Right— Wait. Spar?"

Phainon gobbles up the rest of the sandwich. The soft, milky bread goes wonderfully with the strawberries and cream. "This is good… Yeah! We've been sparring everyday, that's what I was talking about?"

Castorice blinks at him, before her face goes tomato-red. "R—right! A spar! Ahaha, of course!"

Phainon watches in confusion as she turns her face away to dab at it with a handkerchief. He's about to offer her some water, but she spins around to say, "Let's change the topic."

"Ah? But Mydei…"

It's not that he doesn't want to spar Mydei. Phainon thinks that Mydei looks terribly attractive bearing the scars and bruises on his body, as deranged as the thought is. It looks like the night sky, stars scattered across the galaxy infinitely and far too many to count. It's even better to know that it's Phainon that put those on him, marks that show that Phainon is the one who's able to best Mydei.

It, unfortunately, inflicts some other ideas into his head too. His romanticised obsession with Mydei has gotten even stronger with the recollection of memories, the desires turning less than innocent each time he sees Mydei. That possessiveness reels in his head, clamping down onto his every thought when he thinks of Mydei, and only Mydei.

It's his desires that pushed him into agreeing to the countless spars that are hurting Mydei. Phainon knows he should put a stop to it now, before he lets himself unravel even further.

"I think I should apologise to him about it. But I don't know how to make it so that he doesn't try to flip it against me and goad me into another fight."

"I'm not sure if apologies would work on Lord Mydei…"

Phainon grumbles into his cup. "I figured that too. It's not like I don't want to spar him—it's a great distraction from my own mind, really—but seeing him all bruised up and exhausted beneath me is getting a little difficult to handle."

"I think I've lost the conversation again, Lord Phainon."

"Can't you ask Hyacine to get him to stop?" Phainon turns around to pout at her. "Surely he'll listen to someone well-versed in healing, right? Mydei doesn't like upsetting her either."

Castorice, somehow, turns even redder than before. "Ah… Why can't you ask her yourself?"

"Haven't you been hanging out with her everyday? Even when I text her, she tells me she's busy with you as an excuse."

He tilts his head in confusion while Castorice buries her face in her hands.

Phainon managed to weasel out of a spar by saying he's spending time with Castorice. The very next morning, there's a bang on his door, even before the Action Hour arrives.

"This man can't be serious," Phainon mutters to himself, half-dazed from sleep. He stumbles out of bed with an embarrassing lack of balance, only bothering to drag on a pair of pants before he goes to open the door.

In his sleep-addled mind, Mydeimos is beauty incarnate. An image of gold and red that makes his gut churn with need. If he were awoken by the scoff Mydei lets out, he might have reached forward to pull Mydei into a desperate kiss.

"You look like shit, Deliverer."

"Why are you calling me that again? Also, have you heard of the concept of sleep? Most people would be courteous enough to not interrupt someone amidst their rest."

"Phainon," Mydei says, "the best way to be rejuvenated is to partake in a round of battle. Put on a shirt and stop lazing about."

Phainon pointedly looks down at Mydei's shirtlessness, before meeting his eyes. "Is your idea of rejuvenation getting pounded into the cement and bleeding from every inch of your body?"

"That won't happen this time."

"That's what you said the last five times."

"Are you chickening out already, Phainon?" Mydei huffs, crossing his arms. There's an array of scars and bruises on them, all in varying stages of healing.

Phainon doesn't even feel bad when he shuts the door on Mydei. This is a problem for three-quints-later Phainon.

Bathing with the rest of the Chrysos Heirs is quite the rare occasion these days, but a series of pathetic messages from Phainon always does well to convince Aglaea into giving into his whims. Even if it earns him a scolding after.

Castorice never hesitates to join them now, with her touch now warm and soothing. Hyacine said she would pop by when she heard Phainon's complaints about Mydei's current behaviour, seeming way too eager to have the opportunity to rip Mydei a new one.

Aglaea and Cipher were already in the baths when Phainon arrives—he squints at Cipher in confusion. While Aglaea is soaking in the bath, Cipher is still sitting by the side of the bath, legs kicking waves into the golden water.

"Why are you here? I thought cats hate water."

Aglaea lets out a snort as Cipher turns away with a growl. "What I hate is getting my tail wet! It takes way too long to dry."

"My question wasn't answered, I believe."

"Cifera saw your texts on my teleslate and wouldn't stop laughing," Aglaea says, "then she decided she wanted to join in on the conversation herself."

"Not to help you, of course! I just want to know how the little prince is faring now that he can't throw himself in front of a blade whenever he likes!"

Phainon groans, stepping into the water. "Don't remind me. I think babysitting a toddler might be less stressful than this."

"Have you tried setting your boundaries with him? If he doesn't care for his own well-being, then make it known that you do not feel comfortable with his requests."

"I don't think Mydei is aware of that word's meaning. He'll say that it isn't in the Kremnoan dictionary or something."

"You could at least have the decency to mock me to my face instead of Lady Aglaea." A hand buries into his tussled hair and tugs, making Phainon jump and shriek.

Cipher is crumpled into a laughing fit by the time Phainon frees his poor scalp from Mydei's hand, Aglaea covering her face with one hand as she sighs. The ache of his head is enough to distract him from the embarrassment, turning to glare at Mydei as the man sits in the water beside him.

"Are you trying to turn me bald?! Leave my hair alone!"

"It would do you well to learn when to shut up if you wish to keep it, then." Mydei swats Phainon's hand away from his hair, way too long and fluffy for Phainon not to pull.

Cipher scrambles to sit back up, leaning forward to squint at Mydei. "Stand up, little lion."

The rippling of water beside Phainon splashes the warmth on his chest. Phainon glances up to Mydei tousling his hair into a bun as his chest is exposed, showing off the numerous bruises and cuts inflicted onto his skin.

"Oh, that's bad. Seamstress, it was never this bad." Cipher claps her hands excitedly, kicking water in Phainon's direction.

"I don't understand what's the fuss about," Mydei grumbles, sinking back into the bath. "Phainon's worse off than me, he just dresses too modestly."
